notes.quote: It was one of those countless "musts" that had worn me out and kept me from sleeping. It makes no difference whether the "must" is small or large
notes.reader_gets: Both mentions use the quoted bare word "must" as a noun, so what wears him out is the command itself.

notes.quote: it is not I who command them but they who already command me
notes.reader_gets: "Already" signals that the takeover has happened, but it sits oddly in English and the reversal only half reads as something lived through.

notes.quote: the slave of this many-headed beast
notes.reader_gets: The many-headed creature is a beast, which sets up the later human-beast echoes.

notes.quote: If only I could get away from it for a while
notes.reader_gets: He wishes only to escape it. Nothing about becoming free answers the word "slave".

notes.quote: for a while
notes.reader_gets: He wants release only for a time, as a respite.

notes.quote: If only I could get away from it for a while, forget it, rest.
notes.reader_gets: This is a longing, clearly a wish and not a plan.

notes.quote: what matters is that each time it demands my attention, that it is not I who command them but they who already command me
notes.reader_gets: Two "that"-clauses are stacked with only a comma between them, and the pronoun slips from "it" to "them", so the sentence reads as translated.

notes.quote: Because life comes at me ceaselessly and relentlessly, like a wave onto a shore.
notes.reader_gets: The opening "Because" explains the tiredness he has just declared.

notes.quote: life comes at me ceaselessly and relentlessly, like a wave onto a shore
notes.reader_gets: "Comes at me" makes life an assailant striking him, as a wave strikes the shore.

notes.quote: Not only my own life, but other people's too.
notes.reader_gets: The other life is explicitly that of other people.

notes.quote: And after all, do I even know where my own life ends and another's begins?
notes.reader_gets: A first-person admission that he does not know where the boundary lies.

notes.quote: I cannot get past a human being.
notes.reader_gets: Roughly that people block his way and he cannot avoid them, but "get past" is an odd fit and could also suggest getting over or overtaking.

notes.quote: I cannot be alone.
notes.reader_gets: He cannot have solitude, with no sense of loneliness.

notes.quote: I cannot get past a human being.
notes.reader_gets: It stays an inability, something he cannot do.

notes.quote: I cannot be alone.
notes.reader_gets: It stays an inability, something he cannot be.

notes.quote: I cannot get past a human being. I cannot be alone. I confess I envy the planets: they have their orbits, and nothing stands in their way. Whereas on mine I meet a person everywhere and always.
notes.reader_gets: "A human being" and "a person" read as one individual, not as humankind in general.

notes.quote: Whereas on mine
notes.reader_gets: "Mine" clearly refers back to orbits, so this is his own path set against the planets'.

notes.quote: Whereas on mine I meet a person everywhere and always.
notes.reader_gets: A "Whereas" clause stands alone as a sentence, so the closing contrast reads as translated.

notes.quote: It is you who clothed the earth in stone and iron, you who through the windows of houses
notes.reader_gets: The cleft "It is you who… you who…" points at the addressee as the culprit.

notes.quote: you who through the windows of houses, thousands of black mouths, breathe out your stench forever
notes.reader_gets: The windows and the mouth aside are wedged before the verb, and "forever" trails at the end, so it reads as translated.

notes.quote: clothed the earth in stone and iron
notes.reader_gets: The earth is a body dressed in a garment of stone and iron.

notes.quote: You lash the holy silence of the earth
notes.reader_gets: The silence is flogged with a lash.

notes.quote: the holy silence of the earth
notes.reader_gets: The earth's sacred silence, the absence of sound.

notes.quote: Like an animal.
notes.reader_gets: A neutral animal comparison, with no sense of a wild or savage beast.

notes.quote: your bestial instincts
notes.reader_gets: The instincts are beast-like and savage, not mere natural drives.

notes.quote: your eyes, curious and greedy, crawl into me
notes.reader_gets: The eyes are prying and eager to see into him.

notes.quote: I cannot get past you... I cannot be alone...
notes.reader_gets: Block 1's two lines come back almost verbatim as a refrain.

notes.quote: I cannot get past you...
notes.reader_gets: Coming after "you stand in my way", it clearly means he cannot get by or avoid the addressee.

notes.quote: I cannot be alone...
notes.reader_gets: The state of solitude he wants.

notes.quote: you climb inside me
notes.reader_gets: An intrusion, but "climb inside" lacks the crude, creeping, unwelcome colour.

notes.quote: Into my heart, as into your own hiding place, you throw
notes.reader_gets: "Hiding place" leans toward a place where one hides oneself, so the sense of a store for its things is only partly there.

notes.quote: as into your own hiding place
notes.reader_gets: The place is explicitly the addressee's own.

notes.quote: What do you care that you torment me?
notes.reader_gets: The addressee is indifferent to tormenting him.

notes.quote: like a vampire
notes.reader_gets: A vampire as a familiar type.

notes.quote: your countless "musts,"
notes.reader_gets: A quoted word of obligation laid on him.

notes.quote: your countless "musts,"
notes.reader_gets: The same quoted "musts" as in block 0.

notes.quote: your endless "you have tos."
notes.reader_gets: A second-person command spoken to him, distinct from "musts".

notes.quote: I live not as I wish, but as you tell me in your countless "musts," your endless "you have tos."
notes.reader_gets: The meaning comes through, but the plural "you have tos" and "tell me in" read as translated.

notes.quote: People have worn me out.
notes.reader_gets: He is exhausted by people, the same weariness as in block 0.

notes.quote: I am sick of being an inn
notes.reader_gets: He is a roadside lodging open to all comers.

notes.quote: those creatures
notes.reader_gets: "Creatures" is contemptuous in tone, but it is the generic word the check excludes, so it does not clearly class them below people.

notes.quote: Throw out the litterers along with the litter.
notes.reader_gets: They are named by their act of littering and thrown out with it.

notes.quote: Throw out the litterers along with the litter.
notes.reader_gets: His own imperative order.

notes.quote: Air out the house!
notes.reader_gets: An exclamatory command.

notes.quote: Throw out the litterers along with the litter.
notes.reader_gets: A crisp, natural English imperative that snaps shut.

notes.quote: the joy of being alone
notes.reader_gets: Being alone is itself the joy he longs for.

notes.quote: being alone
notes.reader_gets: "Alone" names the plain state of having no one with him, with no sense of sadness.

notes.quote: being alone
notes.reader_gets: "Alone" echoes "I cannot be alone" from blocks 1 and 2, so the refrain is heard.

notes.quote: Who will grant me
notes.reader_gets: An appeal to an unnamed giver, with a psalm-like ring.

notes.quote: How I used to long for them
notes.reader_gets: "Them" is an open plural pronoun with no referent supplied, which the next blocks resolve as the nights.

notes.quote: at times
notes.reader_gets: The longing came only on some occasions.

notes.quote: people lay in wait for me there too
notes.reader_gets: Sleep is one more place where people reach him.

notes.quote: You bring me your sufferings even here?
notes.reader_gets: "Even" goes with "here", so suffering follows him into this refuge.

notes.quote: lay in wait for me
notes.reader_gets: A predatory ambush.

notes.quote: in a fantastic net
notes.reader_gets: A net, a thing made for catching.

notes.quote: fantastic
notes.reader_gets: "Fantastic" can read as dreamlike, but its everyday sense of "wonderful" pulls against the dread.

notes.quote: tried to pour into my ears and my heart what they themselves were full of
notes.reader_gets: Natural English: they try to fill him with what fills them.

notes.quote: Your vileness?
notes.reader_gets: A second, separate and repulsive thing after the suffering.

notes.quote: Your vileness?
notes.reader_gets: "Vileness" means moral loathsomeness, clearly worse than suffering.

notes.quote: Leave me in peace...
notes.reader_gets: A brush-off aimed at the intruder.

notes.quote: Leave me in peace...
notes.reader_gets: The plea names peace.

notes.quote: Leave me in peace...
notes.reader_gets: The dismissal and the plea for peace are one idiom.

notes.quote: at night
notes.reader_gets: A general habitual condition of his nights, not one particular night.

notes.quote: So it was
notes.reader_gets: It points back and sums up the scene as how things were.

notes.quote: So it was at night.
notes.reader_gets: Nothing is restated.

notes.quote: So it was at night.
notes.reader_gets: A flat, curt statement with no added feeling.

notes.quote: So it was at night.
notes.reader_gets: A crisp, literary but natural English coda.

notes.quote: whenever I felt the shadow of a person behind me
notes.reader_gets: He senses the shadow behind him; he does not see it.

notes.quote: the shadow of a person
notes.reader_gets: What he perceives is the shadow itself.

notes.quote: raced toward me
notes.reader_gets: The flood comes straight at him.

notes.quote: the roaring torrents of human life
notes.reader_gets: The flood roars, an audible beast-like sound.

notes.quote: and listened with disgust to the roaring torrents of human life that raced toward me like wild horses
notes.reader_gets: The stresses fall irregularly (LIS-tened with dis-GUST to the ROAR-ing TOR-rents of HU-man LIFE), with no run of four triple-beat stresses, so it reads as ordinary prose.

notes.quote: and listened with disgust to the roaring torrents of human life that raced toward me like wild horses from every street of the city
notes.reader_gets: A fluent English sentence: the disgust phrase sits naturally after the verb, and "from every street" reads as the torrents' source.

notes.quote: The train rushed on, full of human din.
notes.reader_gets: A terse, natural opening line.

notes.quote: the city was stretching its iron hand out into the countryside after me
notes.reader_gets: The city reaches out after him.

notes.quote: its iron hand
notes.reader_gets: An iron hand reaches after him.

notes.quote: would the hand open its iron fingers
notes.reader_gets: The hand's fingers might open.

notes.quote: clack its bones
notes.reader_gets: The noise comes from the hand's bones.

notes.quote: in vain
notes.reader_gets: The hand's movement is futile.

notes.quote: Could I really tear myself from this outcry
notes.reader_gets: "Really" marks his near-disbelief.

notes.quote: this outcry
notes.reader_gets: A voice raised in pain or fright, not just noise.

notes.quote: the unpeopled green expanses
notes.reader_gets: The land is explicitly without people.

notes.quote: green expanses
notes.reader_gets: Open countryside, not parkland.

notes.quote: Would they close behind me, and the iron hand clack its bones in vain?
notes.reader_gets: The image comes through, but the elided "and the iron hand clack its bones" reads stilted and translated.

notes.quote: And would there be silence around me and within me?
notes.reader_gets: Silence, the absence of sound, around him and within him.

notes.quote: so simply and unnoticed
notes.reader_gets: The release slipped by without his noticing, but pairing the adverb "simply" with the participle "unnoticed" reads slightly translated.

notes.quote: I did not hear silence
notes.reader_gets: What he misses is silence.

notes.quote: I did not hear silence
notes.reader_gets: A verb of hearing, which block 13's suddenly heard silence answers.

notes.quote: strangers' voices
notes.reader_gets: The voices belong to other people.

notes.quote: it was drowned out by strangers' voices, petty, useless words, like splinters and straw on spring floodwaters...
notes.reader_gets: The comma chain is carried over, so "petty, useless words" and the simile trail as a loose list.

notes.quote: clickety-clack-clack...
notes.reader_gets: The wheel noise is sounded out as a sound-word.

notes.quote: clickety-clack-clack...
notes.reader_gets: The homely sing-song "clickety-clack", not a hard, crashing iron noise.

notes.quote: clickety-clack-clack... our division was stationed there then... clickety-clack-clack...
notes.reader_gets: The noise keeps cutting in between the scraps of talk.

notes.quote: Where are you going?.. tickets, please...
notes.reader_gets: Bare scraps of talk with no speech tags.

notes.quote: a lady I know
notes.reader_gets: A personal acquaintance of the speaker's.

notes.quote: suffered from her heart for fifteen years
notes.reader_gets: A long-standing bodily heart condition.

notes.quote: our division was stationed there then
notes.reader_gets: A military posting.

notes.quote: Some green chaos
notes.reader_gets: "Some" marks the green mass as something he cannot quite identify.

notes.quote: caught the carriage by all its wheels
notes.reader_gets: Every wheel is seized.

notes.quote: there was so much sky here
notes.reader_gets: The sky is an amount, an excess of it.

notes.quote: my eyes drowned in it as in a sea
notes.reader_gets: The eyes go under as in deep water.

notes.quote: my eyes drowned in it as in a sea and searched
notes.reader_gets: The simple past "drowned" reads as a completed event, not a drowning still in progress.

notes.quote: searched for something to catch hold of
notes.reader_gets: The eyes scan the view for something.

notes.quote: something to catch hold of
notes.reader_gets: They seek a hold, as a drowning man would.

notes.quote: searched for something to catch hold of
notes.reader_gets: Looking and grasping fuse in one phrase.

notes.quote: And were helpless.
notes.reader_gets: The paragraph ends on helplessness as the outcome of the search.

notes.quote: And were helpless.
notes.reader_gets: A bare verdict with no reason or elaboration.

notes.quote: my eyes drowned in it as in a sea and searched for something to catch hold of. And were helpless.
notes.reader_gets: The subjectless closing sentence and "as in a sea" read as translated.

notes.quote: The white walls of the house restore my senses.
notes.reader_gets: The walls bring him back to himself from his daze.

notes.quote: the wide green yard
notes.reader_gets: The house's yard.

notes.quote: a great silence
notes.reader_gets: Silence, an absence of sound.

notes.quote: I heard a great silence
notes.reader_gets: He perceives the silence by hearing it.

notes.quote: It filled the whole yard, lurked in the trees, lay in the deep blue spaces.
notes.reader_gets: "It" clearly refers to the silence, not the cuckoo.

notes.quote: lurked in the trees
notes.reader_gets: The silence is hidden and watchful in the trees.

notes.quote: lay in the deep blue spaces
notes.reader_gets: The silence lies at rest over the expanses.

notes.quote: the pounding of my own heart
notes.reader_gets: A loud, hammering heart.

notes.quote: my own heart
notes.reader_gets: "Own" stresses that the heart is his.

notes.quote: filled with darkness to the brim
notes.reader_gets: "To the brim" makes the darkness a fluid filling the rooms like containers.

notes.quote: to the brim
notes.reader_gets: The rooms are full right to the top.

notes.quote: They press in around my room.
notes.reader_gets: The dark rooms close in on his room like a hostile force.

notes.quote: leak out through the cracks
notes.reader_gets: The light could drain away like a liquid.

notes.quote: the lamplight will all leak out
notes.reader_gets: "All" goes with the light: the whole of it could leak away.

notes.quote: Quiet and empty
notes.reader_gets: "Empty" is general emptiness, not an explicit absence of people.

notes.quote: beyond my wall
notes.reader_gets: The something is on the far side of his own wall.

notes.quote: What is it?
notes.reader_gets: The question asks only what it is, with no pointer to the place.

notes.quote: I can sense the solidity and shape of the furniture
notes.reader_gets: He senses the furniture bodily; he neither hears nor sees it.

notes.quote: the creak of the floor under its weight
notes.reader_gets: The floor creaks.

notes.quote: the furniture sunk at the bottom of the black darkness
notes.reader_gets: The furniture is submerged at the bottom of the dark, as of deep water.

notes.quote: drown in the black darkness myself
notes.reader_gets: He would drown in the dark.

notes.quote: stay where you are, rest in peace
notes.reader_gets: The furniture is told both to stay put and to rest.

notes.quote: rest in peace
notes.reader_gets: The graveside formula.

notes.quote: Well, stay where you are, rest in peace.
notes.reader_gets: The graveside ring comes from the formula itself, with nothing spelled out.

notes.quote: a soulless object
notes.reader_gets: An object without a soul.

notes.quote: a voiceless, motionless calm
notes.reader_gets: He would become calm itself, a noun state, not merely be calm.

notes.quote: I know that if I were to walk into the dark rooms like this and strike a match, everything would leap at once into its place
notes.reader_gets: Grammatically sound, but "like this" is an odd calque for "just so" and leaves a translated trace.

notes.quote: everything would leap at once into its place
notes.reader_gets: The things leap back to their places.

notes.quote: my eye would have time to catch
notes.reader_gets: The glimpse depends on his eye being quick enough.

notes.quote: the image of people, pale, indistinct, as if from tapestries, all those who left their faces in the mirrors
notes.reader_gets: The adjectives are stranded after the noun and "as if from tapestries" is a calque, so it reads as translated.

notes.quote: Well, there! What nonsense.
notes.reader_gets: "Well, there!" reads a little stilted, almost as if he were pointing at something, though "What nonsense" carries the dismissal.

notes.quote: You wanted quiet and solitude
notes.reader_gets: Solitude, being without people, is named separately from the quiet.

notes.quote: You do not believe in solitude?
notes.reader_gets: The doubt falls on the solitude alone.

notes.quote: solitude
notes.reader_gets: Solitude is the welcome thing he wished for.

notes.quote: You shake your head! You do not believe in solitude?
notes.reader_gets: The exclaimed head-shake and the abstract "believe in solitude" sound stiff and translated.

notes.quote: Do I know? Can I know... Can I be sure
notes.reader_gets: He admits he does not know and cannot be sure.

notes.quote: Can I be sure that the door will not swing open... just a little, with a faint creak, and out of the unknown darkness, so deep and endless, people will not begin to come...
notes.reader_gets: He fears the door will open and people will come out.

notes.quote: all those who laid into my heart, as into their own hiding place, their hopes
notes.reader_gets: "Laid into" first reads as "attacked", and "hiding place" leans toward a place to hide oneself, so the image of a store for their things comes through only with effort.

notes.quote: as into their own hiding place
notes.reader_gets: The place is theirs.

notes.quote: All those I cannot get past, who have worn me out...
notes.reader_gets: The refrain of the people he cannot avoid comes back.

notes.quote: Well, well! How many of you there are...
notes.reader_gets: Mock-hospitable surprise at their number.

notes.quote: This is you, whose blood drained out through a small hole from a soldier's bullet, and this is you... dry specimens:
notes.reader_gets: The stilted "This is you, whose…" frame and the dangling label read as translated.

notes.quote: dry specimens
notes.reader_gets: Collection or laboratory objects, dried and kept for study.

notes.quote: how they hanged twelve of you at once... Twelve of you...
notes.reader_gets: The number is given bare, with no intensifier stressing it as large.

notes.quote: Twelve of you...
notes.reader_gets: He returns to the figure and dwells on it.

notes.quote: Twelve of you... and I yawned.
notes.reader_gets: The yawn comes last, as the reveal.

notes.quote: and I yawned.
notes.reader_gets: A bare yawn with no explanation.

notes.quote: I ate up the news of a row of white sacks with a ripe plum
notes.reader_gets: "Ate up the news" reads as devouring it eagerly, and the plum as an accompaniment, not as something sweet taken to cover a bitter taste.

notes.quote: I simply took, you know, a wonderful juicy plum in my fingers
notes.reader_gets: Casual table talk with conversational asides to the dead.

notes.quote: horror has sucked all the blood out of me
notes.reader_gets: The horror has sucked all his blood out of him.

notes.quote: like a bloody phantom
notes.reader_gets: A blood-stained ghost, but "bloody" can ring as a British oath.

notes.quote: Pass on!
notes.reader_gets: A command to move on past him.

notes.quote: And people keep coming.
notes.reader_gets: They keep coming despite his plea.

notes.quote: One after another, a second and a third
notes.reader_gets: He counts them off to a third, but tacking the count onto "one after another" reads awkwardly.

notes.quote: and so without end
notes.reader_gets: After the count, the sequence runs out into endlessness.

notes.quote: near and strange
notes.reader_gets: Close people set against strangers, but "near and strange" is an odd, un-English pairing.

notes.quote: all of them shout into my ears the cry of their life or their death
notes.reader_gets: A forceful line with no cognate echo, natural enough.

notes.quote: leave on my soul the prints of their soles
notes.reader_gets: Lasting marks remain on his soul.

notes.quote: the prints of their soles
notes.reader_gets: The marks are made by feet.

notes.quote: leave on my soul the prints of their soles
notes.reader_gets: Footprints on the soul in one image, sharpened by the soul/soles play.

notes.quote: and shout: no admittance here!
notes.reader_gets: A single future outcry, with nothing marking that it goes on.

notes.quote: no admittance here!
notes.reader_gets: The formula of a posted sign.

notes.quote: no admittance here!
notes.reader_gets: A bar on entry, with no hint of a fee.

notes.quote: A cuckoo is calling.
notes.reader_gets: The bird is calling.

notes.quote: A cuckoo is calling.
notes.reader_gets: A plain calling verb with no hint of hammering, so the hammer in the next sentence comes from nowhere.

notes.quote: A cuckoo is calling.
notes.reader_gets: No single word carries both the call and the blows.

notes.quote: with a little hammer
notes.reader_gets: The hammer is small.

notes.quote: a great crystal bell
notes.reader_gets: The bell is large.

notes.quote: It strikes with a little hammer on a great crystal bell
notes.reader_gets: Told as what the bird does, not as a likeness.

notes.quote: and sows silence over the grass
notes.reader_gets: The cuckoo's calling produces the silence.

notes.quote: sows silence
notes.reader_gets: The silence is sown like seed.

notes.quote: sows silence
notes.reader_gets: Silence, the keyword, returns.

notes.quote: the green yard, which has already swallowed up my room
notes.reader_gets: The house's known yard, already overrunning his room.

notes.quote: merry green
notes.reader_gets: The green is glad.

notes.quote: iron chains clank
notes.reader_gets: The chains are iron.

notes.quote: dogs bark furiously
notes.reader_gets: A furious vocal uproar.

notes.quote: their long shaggy wool leaps with them
notes.reader_gets: The wool has its own leaping.

notes.quote: Red eyes leap, a broad forehead leaps, and white furry leggings.
notes.reader_gets: Each part is itself leaping.

notes.quote: the matted tufts on her hindquarters fly after her
notes.reader_gets: The fur flies after the dog as if in pursuit.

notes.quote: Well, what is it, dog...
notes.reader_gets: "What is it" asks what is wrong, and "Well, what is it, Overko" repeats it, as coaxing.

notes.quote: white furry leggings
notes.reader_gets: The leg fur is pictured as a garment.

notes.quote: A fury, all teeth, strains and cannot quite burst out of the deep maw
notes.reader_gets: The fury strains to break out and fails.

notes.quote: and only tosses up a haystack of wool
notes.reader_gets: Only a jolt of the dog's own woolly bulk.

notes.quote: A fury, all teeth, strains and cannot quite burst out of the deep maw, and only tosses up a haystack of wool.
notes.reader_gets: A vivid, natural English sentence.

notes.quote: melting fear and hatred together in the fire
notes.reader_gets: The two feelings are fused in the fire like metals.

notes.quote: draw some blood from my calf
notes.reader_gets: Explicit blood.

notes.quote: Perhaps you are angrier at it than at me.
notes.reader_gets: The anger is aimed at the chain more than at him.

notes.quote: it throttles you by the throat and drives your fiery rage back down into it
notes.reader_gets: The final "it" probably means the throat, but it could be taken for the chain.

notes.quote: until they take the chain off you
notes.reader_gets: Unnamed others remove the chain.

notes.quote: off she tears without a thought, blind
notes.reader_gets: Reckless, frantic abandon.

notes.quote: without a thought
notes.reader_gets: Thoughtlessness rather than oblivion; the link to forgetting is faint.

notes.quote: off she tears without a thought, blind
notes.reader_gets: The frenzy and the thoughtlessness sit in the one phrase.

notes.quote: off she tears
notes.reader_gets: "She" suggests a female dog, not Overko.

notes.quote: What, have you forgotten?
notes.reader_gets: The dog has forgotten him.

notes.quote: Well, and what about me? What, have you forgotten?
notes.reader_gets: Quick, natural mock-offence.
